primitives.name: Home Court Performance Shift
primitives.verbatim_quote: Between the 2011-2012 and 2015-2016 seasons, NCAA teams performed better at home compared to on the road in nearly all box score statistics across both genders and all three divisions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H_{\\text{stat}}': 'Home team box score statistic', 'A_{\\text{stat}}': 'Away team box score statistic', '\\Delta_{\\text{stat}}': '\\frac{H_{\\text{stat}} - A_{\\text{stat}}}{A_{\\text{stat}}} \\times 100\\% \\quad \\text{(percentage increase)}'}
primitives.assumptions: Statistical independence of performance metrics across teams, constant bias across seasons.

layer2.telemetry: Mean percentage difference in box score statistics between home and away teams.

primitives.name: Scorekeeper Bias Factor
primitives.verbatim_quote: We present evidence that scorekeepers tend to have greater home team biases when observing men compared to women, higher divisions compared to lower divisions, and stronger teams compared to weaker teams.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B_{\\text{sk}}': 'Scorekeeper bias coefficient', 'T_{\\text{strength}}': 'Team strength index', 'G_{\\text{gender}}': 'Gender indicator (0/1)', 'D_{\\text{div}}': 'Division level (1–3)'}
primitives.assumptions: Bias is linearly dependent on team strength and categorical gender/division.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( B_{\text{sk}} \to 0 \), indicating no systematic bias.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's state transition kernel for observer bias in real-time scoring.
layer2.telemetry: Regression coefficient for home team bias in box score reporting.

primitives.name: Referee Attendance Impact
primitives.verbatim_quote: Finally, we present statistically significant results indicating referee decisions are impacted by attendance, with larger crowds resulting in greater bias in favor of the home team.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{\\text{bias}}': 'Referee bias magnitude', 'A_{\\text{crowd}}': 'Crowd attendance count', 'H_{\\text{team}}': 'Home team identifier'}
primitives.assumptions: Referee bias increases monotonically with crowd size and is conditional on home team.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( R_{\text{bias}} \to 0 \), indicating no influence of attendance.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's dynamic decision tree for officiating variance under crowd pressure.
layer2.telemetry: Coefficient of attendance effect on foul calls and game outcomes.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that home court advantage manifests not just in win-loss records but in measurable box score differentials. This is formalized as a stochastic shift \( \Delta_{\text{stat}} \) in performance metrics, where \( H_{\text{stat}} > A_{\text{stat}} \) indicates a home advantage. The regression-adjusted model isolates this shift from confounding variables like team strength and possessions. Scorekeeper bias \( B_{\text{sk}} \) is modeled as a function of team strength and categorical identifiers, capturing potential systematic misreporting. Referee bias \( R_{\text{bias}} \) is linked to attendance, implying a non-linear feedback loop in game dynamics. These primitives form a dual structure: one for static performance shifts and another for dynamic behavioral influences. Failure modes include zero-bias limits, where \( \Delta_{\text{stat}} \to 0 \), or extreme bias where \( B_{\text{sk}} \to \infty \), leading to invalid statistical inference.
